newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent ends down 19 cts, clings to support at $20.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent ends down 19 cts, clings to support at $20.

text.p: IPE Brent crude futures closed down 19 cents on Friday on weaker NYMEX crude and speculative selling from New York, traders said.

Front month May Brent last traded at $20.00 a barrel and settled at $19.99, closing a spread that had hovered around five to seven cents for much of the day. June Brent last traded at $20.00 but settled in contango at $20.01.
The May Brent/NYMEX crude spread finished at $1.52, around six cents softer than morning levels.
Repeated attacks on May at $20.00 by U.S. sellers in the last three hours of business found solid support at the psychologically important number, backed by late market-on-close short-covering.
Traders said there was no fundamental news that made a lasting impression on market direction.
"We had very good support at $20 and that is an indication to me that we are still in business at higher levels next week," a trader said.
IPE gas oil ended down $2.50 a tonne at the intraday low. May WTI was down 33 cents at $21.52 a barrel. Gasoline finished up 0.02 cent at 67.60 cents a gallon.
Front month April gas oil settled at $170.75 a tonne, down $2.50.
Futures weakened in mid-afternoon by an announcement of an agreement by Russia to develop seven billion to eight billion barrels of reserves in southern Iraq.
Traders reported some nervousness at remarks by Russian Energy Minister Pyotr Rodinov in Baghdad that execution of the contract would happen regardless of U.N. Gulf War sanctions against Iraq.
Traders said the nervousness faded when it became clear the contract was a long-term development contract and did not herald short-term growth in Iraqi oil production or exports.
